clue.text: Top gambling game

parts.note: a spinning top with lettered sides, spun for stakes, whose face tells each player to pay in or take out of the pool

explanation.surface: A heading for the leading game of chance in a casino.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' reads as 'best', but it is the toy: the game is played with a small many-sided spinning top.
explanation.definitionFit: The game takes its name from the instructions printed on the faces of the teetotum it is played with.

clue.text: Trudged along full of stuffing

definitions.meaning: to pad is to walk steadily on foot
filled with soft material, like a cushion

explanation.surface: Someone plodded on after a large dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To pad is to walk with steady soft steps, and something padded is filled with soft wadding.

clue.text: Is inclined to make charges

definitions.meaning: leans or slopes to one side
in jousting, knights ride at each other with lances

explanation.surface: Someone tends to run up bills.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilt is a slope, and also a knight's charge with a lance in a joust.

clue.text: He writes for TV sole information

indicators.note: formation means the letters are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A television writer has exclusive inside knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'information' splits into 'in' and 'formation': the latter rearranges TV SOLE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelist is an author of works of long prose fiction.

clue.text: This line is omitted by the cast

indicators.note: omitted says the word is is left out of the word before it

parts.note: a row is a line of people or things

explanation.surface: An actor's speech is dropped by the company putting on the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is omitted' takes IS out of 'This', leaving TH; ROW follows. The theatrical 'line' and 'cast' are the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast a stone or a net is to fling it.

clue.text: Abducted by a 3

definitions.meaning: carried off by force and held
a book by an author, the answer to 3-down: Robert Louis Stevenson's adventure novel

explanation.surface: Someone was carried off by a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to 3-down, a writer of novels; Stevenson's 1886 novel bears the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Seized and carried away illegally; also the Stevenson novel about David Balfour.

clue.text: Work on address to a Manx cat

parts.note: O is the old vocative form of address, as in 'O king'

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for the cat loses its final letter

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: Someone writes a piece about speaking to a tailless cat from the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' cuts the last letter from PUSS, giving PUS, because the Manx breed is tailless; O, the address of 'O king', goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is the Latin word used for a numbered composition or other artistic creation.

clue.text: Hit nose shifting casks

parts.note: to punch is to hit with the fist

indicators.note: shifting means the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A blow to the nose sends barrels rolling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' rearranges NOSE into EONS, after PUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Puncheons are large barrels for liquids such as rum or wine.

clue.text: They are beginning to put more acid in the vessel

indicators.note: in means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a vessel
tarter means sharper, more sour

explanation.surface: Some cooks start by adding extra acid to the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: SS, steamship, is the vessel, not a cooking pot; TARTER goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Starters are those who start a race or an enterprise.

clue.text: Failure to supply material

definitions.meaning: a collapse, as of a business or computer
a coarse plain linen fabric used for towels

explanation.surface: Someone fails to deliver some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash is a sudden collapse, and crash is also a rough linen cloth.

clue.text: Rescue someone and get abused in return

indicators.note: returning a word means reading it from its last letter back to its first

parts.note: to be reviled is to be abused with insults

explanation.surface: A rescuer is insulted for their trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' turns REVILED round, letter by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone is to set them free from danger, as in 'deliver us from evil'.

clue.text: Eliot's hero rode out and tumbled

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of rode are put out of their order
tumbled signals that the letters of and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A rider in a George Eliot novel goes out on horseback and falls off.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word has its own anagram signal: 'out' rearranges RODE into DERO and 'tumbled' rearranges AND into NDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Deronda is the title character of George Eliot's last novel.

clue.text: Turner's work held up by this, no doubt

definitions.text: Turner's work held up by this, no doubt

parts.words: Turner's work held up by this, no doubt
parts.note: the painter J. M. W. Turner's canvases stood on a wooden stand while he worked on them

explanation.surface: Something must be delaying the progress of a turner at their lathe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner's work held up' sounds like a craftsman's job delayed; it is the painter's canvas literally held upright.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the upright frame that supports a painting while the artist works.

clue.text: Clueful types know it, as obvious as "a rose is a rose"

definitions.text: Clueful types know it, as obvious as "a rose is a rose"

parts.words: Clueful types know it, as obvious as "a rose is a rose"
parts.note: people in the know understand the true state of things, and Gertrude Stein's line says a thing is simply itself

explanation.surface: Knowing people grasp something as plain as Gertrude Stein's famous tautology.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works twice: knowing people 'know' it, and 'a rose is a rose' says something is what it is.
explanation.definitionFit: To know the real facts of a situation is an idiom built from the tautology 'a thing is what it is'.

clue.text: N.C.O. translated letters for soldier?

indicators.note: translated means the three initials are carried over into a new order

parts.note: a non-commissioned officer, abbreviated by its initials
script is written letters, handwriting

explanation.surface: A sergeant renders some correspondence for a private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges NCO into CON; SCRIPT (written letters) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A conscript is a soldier called up compulsorily rather than one who volunteered.

clue.text: Error in field causes defeat?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a fielder's throw that runs past the stumps, giving extra runs
a toppling of a government or ruler

explanation.surface: A mistake on the battlefield leads to losing the war.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: an overthrow is a fielder's wild return, letting batsmen run extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketing misfield, and the forcible removal of a ruler from power.

clue.text: Gave out rapidly, as the drunkard did, perhaps

definitions.meaning: recited a list quickly and fluently

explanation.surface: Someone distributed things in a hurry, like a staggering drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite a string of facts at speed, and to stagger away from a place.

clue.text: Animal with fur and red head

parts.note: a boa is a long fur or feather stole worn round the neck

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of red is used

explanation.surface: A creature with a coat and a ginger head.
explanation.walkthrough: BOA is the fur stole, not the snake; R is the head (first letter) of 'red'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is an uncastrated male pig, or a wild pig.

clue.text: Gamble on mine products, for example

parts.note: a spec is a speculation, a risky venture

indicators.note: products are things made, so the letters of mine are made into something new

explanation.surface: An investor speculates on shares in mining output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'products' rearranges MINE into IMEN, after SPEC.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a sample or instance taken as typical of its kind.

clue.text: Notorious outburst of patriotism ?

indicators.note: outburst of patriotism puts the second word's piece before the first's

parts.note: the flag stands for patriotic feeling, as in flag-waving
a rant is a loud, angry tirade

explanation.surface: An infamous outpouring of nationalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' puts FLAG, the symbol of patriotism, before RANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means glaringly obvious and shocking, as in a flagrant offence.

clue.text: It's sound but feeble anyway

indicators.note: anyway says the word reads correctly whichever way it is read, forwards or back

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something is healthy but weak all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' suggests 'healthy', set against 'feeble'; it is a noise. 'anyway' says the answer reads either way, a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A peep is a faint, high little noise, so it is a weak kind of utterance.

clue.text: Deadly hostility to mails being collected by the old system

parts.note: a feud is a bitter, often murderous quarrel between families

indicators.note: letters being collected are gathered up and composed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Lethal enmity towards the postal service is fostered by an antiquated set-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being collected' rearranges MAILS into ALISM, which follows FEUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudalism was the medieval European social order of lords, vassals and land held in return for service.

clue.text: Item for boxing contest?

definitions.meaning: one of the sticks sold packed in a small box
a game or competition between sides

explanation.surface: A pair of gloves for a prize fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' is the sport in the surface but is literally packing into a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchstick comes in a matchbox, and a match is a sporting contest.

clue.text: " My men, like grazing on the lawns "(Marlowe)

definitions.text: " My men, like grazing on the lawns "(Marlowe)

parts.words: " My men, like grazing on the lawns "(Marlowe)
parts.note: a gap-fill quotation from Gaveston's speech in Marlowe's Edward II about mythical woodland goat-men

explanation.surface: A line from Christopher Marlowe's play about men in a pastoral scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation, from Marlowe's Edward II, has a word missing between 'like' and 'grazing': the creatures part man, part goat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaveston pictures his men dressed as the goat-legged woodland followers of Bacchus.

clue.text: Residents make bed and tidy grates

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: to tidy is to put things into a different order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Householders are making their beds and cleaning the fireplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tidy' rearranges GRATES into TAGERS, which follows COT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cottagers are people who live in cottages, country dwellers.

clue.text: Island's put up a black

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Elba is the island of Napoleon's exile, here with its possessive s

explanation.surface: An island has set up a dark flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns ELBA'S round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic name for the colour black.

clue.text: Lake has a drawback

indicators.note: back attached to draw tells you to read the run of letters backwards

parts.note: to draw something along is to drag it

explanation.surface: A lake has a disadvantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' reads as a disadvantage, but it splits: 'draw' gives DRAG and 'back' turns A + DRAG round.
explanation.definitionFit: Garda is the largest lake in Italy.

clue.text: In short, boy gets the same music

parts.note: Ron is a shortened form of the boy's name Ronald
do is short for ditto, the same

explanation.surface: Briefly, a lad gets an identical tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' says the boy's name is abbreviated; DO is ditto.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form whose main theme keeps returning between episodes.

clue.text: Its prince chose gold at Belmont

definitions.text: Its prince chose gold at Belmont

parts.words: Its prince chose gold at Belmont
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice, the first suitor at Portia's house in Belmont picks the gold casket and loses her

explanation.surface: A royal suitor makes his choice of casket at Portia's house.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue refers to Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, where Portia's suitors choose between gold, silver and lead caskets.
explanation.definitionFit: The suitor who chose the gold casket is named after his North African country.

clue.text: Learn by cajoling, possibly

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could be set in some other arrangement

explanation.surface: You may pick things up by flattering people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges LEARN BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Blarney is smooth flattering talk meant to win someone over, from the Irish stone said to grant the gift of the gab.

clue.text: This wench is holding information back

indicators.note: back means the letters held there are read from right to left
the two words are holding the answer inside them, across the word break

explanation.surface: A young woman is keeping some intelligence to herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is holding' points to the run SWEN across 'This wench'; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: News is fresh information about recent events.

clue.text: Tender feelings of foes in fact? That's odd

indicators.note: something odd is out of the normal order, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Enemies with warm feelings for each other would be strange indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's odd' rearranges FOES IN FACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Affections are feelings of fondness and warmth towards someone.
